title: Preflight decision lattice and release-notes assembly pipeline for API / Console / Runtime
creator: Maya Chen
description: Create a deterministic preflight decision lattice and an automated assembly pipeline for release notes that coordinates API, Console, and Runtime teams. The goal is to standardize go/no-go signals, ownership handoffs, and a single source-of-truth artifact for release communications so we reduce last-minute confusion during scope lock and cut decisions.
acceptance_criteria: A1: Decision lattice doc (visual + prose) published in Confluence with clear signal thresholds for commit/block/rollback
A2: Release-notes assembly pipeline defined with owners for feature blurb, risk classification, and rollback instructions
A3: Preflight checklist that integrates telemetry sentinels, infra readiness, docs readiness, and legal/compliance signoffs
A4: Run a dry-run with next sprint's candidate = produce release notes artifact and collect signoffs within 48 hours
A5: Post-dry-run retro and action items captured in the ticket
tasks: T1: Draft initial decision lattice visualization and signal table (PM + ENG)
T2: Define release-note schema (title, owners, risk, user-impact, rollback steps, docs link)
T3: Wire up a simple assembly doc in Drive that pulls owners' blurbs via a template
T4: Create preflight checklist with checkboxes for telemetry, perf benchmarks, infra capacity, security scans, and docs
T6: Run dry-run with next candidate and collect signoffs
T7: Capture retro and update pipeline; hand off to release ops
notes: Context: Recent launches suffered from inconsistent risk language in release notes and unclear abort conditions during the scope-lock window.
Design constraints: Keep the lattice lightweight — binary signals (green/yellow/red) that map to explicit actions; avoid >7 signals to preserve human decisionability.
Ops constraint: Assembly must be produce-able as a single artifact that ReleaseOps can paste into the product announcement and external changelog.
Trade-offs considered: Automated signal aggregation vs manual signoff — we'll start with manual signoff for first two runs and iterate toward automation.
